corrections.subject: docs/GUN_PLATFORM_ARC.md, the seed of the platform window list
corrections.was: the platform is seeded with one full-circle window somewhere this packet did not find
corrections.is: the seed exists and its flags are 0: neither traverse nor fire. The authored data settles it. `VehicleClass[265].Platforms[1]` (Turret A) authors the two windows [-145,0] and [0,145] and `Platforms[4]` (Turret D) authors [30,180] and [-180,-30], each leaving the sector its own superstructure blocks uncovered. corrections.subject: docs/UNIT_GUNNERY_PASS.md section 8.7, the director targets

Two producers of miss: 0072F830's per-pellet perturbation of the muzzle direction from the class `Throw` (0.01 on the 133mm turret), and 006DF520 step 10's per-bot error pair from the robot skill descriptor that load_robot_config_00901610 reads out of Robots.lua. Neither is applied, so the run's 161 hits in 215 shots is an upper bound, not a measurement.

A platform's mount point is a model node and this process holds no model. Every gun fires from its unit's pose translation raised by the class `Height`, so a battery has no spread across the hull and a blocked arc is measured from the hull centre rather than from the turret.

entity vtable[0FCh], the sub-entity enumeration step 8.7 expands both director targets into. It is what would let the director's own fire target reach a gun without the recon sweep, and it is why no torpedo fires on this mission.
A shape whose vtable[0] writes a real hull segment into hit+34h. Without one, 00826F10's part damage, roll torque, fire and flooding are all unreachable from a shell.

docs/RECON_SLOT_LISTS.md rule (c), the per-observer detection value, and the sensor tables behind it. This run applies rules (a) and (b) only, so every enemy in class scope is a contact regardless of whether anything has seen it.
